correctness.rationale: The proof decomposes Fourier degree <=2 into radial, one-contrast, and two-contrast orthonormal tensor blocks under conditional uniform Hamming-shell measure. The three radial eigenvalues are squared ambient projection norms of Johnson degree 0,1,2 test functions; the one-contrast ranks and two eigenvalues follow from conditional hypergeometric support; the double-contrast eigenvalue follows from independent centered label conditioning. Exact positive multiplicities sum to binomial(n,2)(q-1)^2; the multiplier nullspace R H<=1 is injectively parameterized and has the remaining dimension 1+n(q-1). The shell density w converts normalized Gram eigenvalues into the concentration eigenvalues. Exact integer matrix powers and annihilating polynomials match the full predicted spectrum in four finite instances; those finite tests are corroborative, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The problem measures complete low-band Fourier sampling from a natural q-ary constant-weight domain; its spectral levels determine all best and worst recoverable modes and optimal quotient conditioning. Uniform exact rank, a complete explicit multiplier kernel, and six structurally different sectors for every q>=3 and every interior k provide meaningful and reusable classification beyond finite recomputation or a routine single inequality. The statement is sharp and describes an entire natural infinite parameter family, while making no unsupported higher-degree or algorithmic performance claims.
